label: copy phase: input t/p, or any copy step of a 3-token sequence
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L). It never fires on original-phase or delimiter steps, or on the first copy output. Within the copy phase it is diffuse, about 2.4% of steps. Three additive tendencies: (1) the fed-back input is t or p (t has 10x lift and carries 34% of mass; p has 3.4x); (2) short sequences, especially L=3, where 45% of copy steps are active; (3) late copy steps (to_go <= 1, 76% of mass) and recall_idx 2. The strongest activations are at step L+2 of L=3 sequences when the input is t or p (e.g. q t 3 <DEL> q [t]). The predicate (copy phase and (L==3 or input in {t,p})) gets about 72% of mass but only 18% precision on dev. Most copy-phase t/p inputs in longer sequences do not fire, and there is a long tail of weak activations on other tokens near the end of long sequences.
